$note: THE NAMING LAYER — the only part of the grammar's terminals a human owns. Everything structural (which columns a Kind has, which commands exist, which effects group into a class) is derived from the ontology by `derive_grammar.py`; this file supplies the words a member would use for what the derivation found, plus the conversational terminals the vault has nothing to say about. `emit.py` validates every entry here against `derived.json` and generates `grammar/lexicon.py` and `crates/candidates/src/canon_terminals.rs` from the pair, so the two parsers cannot drift from each other or from the ontology.
$kindsNote: Kind name -> [logical entity, door]. `emit.py` refuses a pair the doors do not serve. `composite` names further entities whose columns the door hands back on the same row — GRAMMAR.md §2.1 already says the `photos` Kind is `core_content_item`+`media_asset`; writing it here makes the second half checkable instead of implied.
$readerFieldsNote: Facts an app's reader computes and hands back beside the row — GRAMMAR.md §2.2 admits these and named no source, so the source is named here and `emit.py` checks it. A path is checked by finding the field named in a file under `crates/apps/*/src` or an app manifest. `manifest` means the owning app DECLARES it under `derivedFields`, with what computes it and which tables it reads; `emit.py` refuses one no manifest declares. The four that were `harness` are now declared with `computedBy: null` — the product ships no reader for them (DIFF.md B4-B7), and a declared gap is a statement, where `harness` was a shrug.
$verbClassesNote: The CLASS NAME a member says, mapped onto the effect `derive_grammar.py` found in each command's handler SQL. `emit.py` refuses a member that is not a registered command. The entity spellings are the grammar's; where they differ from the one the derivation files the command under, DIFF.md section C says so (`media.delete_asset` takes an `asset_id`).
$sessionNote: Terminals of the CONVERSATION, not of the vault. The ontology has nothing to say about them, so they are declared, not derived — but they are declared ONCE, which is the point.
